bsb.4:32: Solomon composed three thousand proverbs, and his songs numbered a thousand and five.
bsb.4:33: He spoke of trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop growing in the wall, and he taught about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish.
bsb.4:34: So men of all nations came to listen to Solomon’s wisdom, sent by all the kings of the earth, who had heard of his wisdom.
bsb.5:1: Now when Hiram king of Tyre heard that Solomon had been anointed king in his father’s place, he sent envoys to Solomon; for Hiram had always been a friend of David.
bsb.5:2: And Solomon relayed this message to Hiram:
bsb.5:3: “As you are well aware, due to the wars waged on all sides against my father David, he could not build a house for the Name of the LORD his God until the LORD had put his enemies under his feet.
bsb.5:4: But now the LORD my God has given me rest on every side, and there is no adversary or crisis.
bsb.5:5: So behold, I plan to build a house for the Name of the LORD my God, according to what the LORD said to my father David: ‘I will put your son on your throne in your place, and he will build the house for My Name.’
bsb.5:6: Now therefore, order that cedars of Lebanon be cut down for me. My servants will be with your servants, and I will pay your servants whatever wages you set, for you know that there are none among us as skilled in logging as the Sidonians.”
bsb.5:7: When Hiram received Solomon’s message, he rejoiced greatly and said, “Blessed be the LORD this day! He has given David a wise son over this great people!”
bsb.5:8: Then Hiram sent a reply to Solomon, saying: “I have received your message; I will do all you desire regarding the cedar and cypress timber.
bsb.5:9: My servants will haul the logs from Lebanon to the Sea, and I will float them as rafts by sea to the place you specify. There I will separate the logs, and you can take them away. And in exchange, you can meet my needs by providing my household with food.”
bsb.5:10: So Hiram provided Solomon with all the cedar and cypress timber he wanted,
bsb.5:11: and year after year Solomon would provide Hiram with 20,000 cors of wheat as food for his household, as well as 20,000 baths of pure olive oil.
bsb.5:12: And the LORD gave Solomon wisdom, as He had promised him. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a treaty.
bsb.5:13: Then King Solomon conscripted a labor force of 30,000 men from all Israel.
bsb.5:14: He sent them to Lebanon in monthly shifts of 10,000 men, so that they would spend one month in Lebanon and two months at home. And Adoniram was in charge of the forced labor.
bsb.5:15: Solomon had 70,000 porters and 80,000 stonecutters in the mountains,
bsb.5:16: not including his 3,300 foremen who supervised the workers.
bsb.5:17: And the king commanded them to quarry large, costly stones to lay the foundation of the temple with dressed stones.
bsb.5:18: So Solomon’s and Hiram’s builders, along with the Gebalites, quarried the stone and prepared the timber and stone for the construction of the temple.
bsb.6:1: In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites had come out of the land of Egypt, in the month of Ziv, the second month of the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, he began to build the house of the LORD.
bsb.6:2: The house that King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.
bsb.6:3: The portico at the front of the main hall of the temple was twenty cubits long, extending across the width of the temple and projecting out ten cubits in front of the temple.
bsb.6:4: He also had narrow windows framed high in the temple.
bsb.6:5: Against the walls of the temple and the inner sanctuary, Solomon built a chambered structure around the temple, in which he constructed the side rooms.
bsb.6:6: The bottom floor was five cubits wide, the middle floor six cubits, and the third floor seven cubits. He also placed offset ledges around the outside of the temple, so that nothing would be inserted into its walls.
bsb.6:7: The temple was constructed using finished stones cut at the quarry, so that no hammer or chisel or any other iron tool was heard in the temple while it was being built.
bsb.6:8: The entrance to the bottom floor was on the south side of the temple. A stairway led up to the middle level, and from there to the third floor.
bsb.6:9: So Solomon built the temple and finished it, roofing it with beams and planks of cedar.
bsb.6:10: He built chambers all along the temple, each five cubits high and attached to the temple with beams of cedar.
bsb.6:11: Then the word of the LORD came to Solomon, saying:
bsb.6:12: “As for this temple you are building, if you walk in My statutes, carry out My ordinances, and keep all My commandments by walking in them, I will fulfill through you the promise I made to your father David.
bsb.6:13: And I will dwell among the Israelites and will not abandon My people Israel.”
bsb.6:14: So Solomon built the temple and finished it.
bsb.6:15: He lined the interior walls with cedar paneling from the floor of the temple to the ceiling, and he covered the floor with cypress boards.
bsb.6:16: He partitioned off the twenty cubits at the rear of the temple with cedar boards from floor to ceiling to form within the temple an inner sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.
bsb.6:17: And the main hall in front of this room was forty cubits long.
bsb.6:18: The cedar paneling inside the temple was carved with gourds and open flowers. Everything was cedar; not a stone could be seen.
bsb.6:19: Solomon also prepared the inner sanctuary within the temple to set the ark of the covenant of the LORD there.
bsb.6:20: The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high. He overlaid the inside with pure gold, and he also overlaid the altar of cedar.
bsb.6:21: So Solomon overlaid the inside of the temple with pure gold, and he extended gold chains across the front of the inner sanctuary, which was overlaid with gold.
bsb.6:22: So he overlaid with gold the whole interior of the temple, until everything was completely finished. He also overlaid with gold the entire altar that belonged to the inner sanctuary.
bsb.6:23: In the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim, each ten cubits high, out of olive wood.
bsb.6:24: One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long, and the other wing was five cubits long as well. So the full wingspan was ten cubits.
bsb.6:25: The second cherub also measured ten cubits; both cherubim had the same size and shape,
bsb.6:26: and the height of each cherub was ten cubits.
bsb.6:27: And he placed the cherubim inside the innermost room of the temple. Since their wings were spread out, the wing of the first cherub touched one wall, while the wing of the second cherub touched the other wall, and in the middle of the room their wingtips touched.
bsb.6:28: He also overlaid the cherubim with gold.
bsb.6:29: Then he carved the walls all around the temple, in both the inner and outer sanctuaries, with carved engravings of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers.
bsb.6:30: And he overlaid the temple floor with gold in both the inner and outer sanctuaries.
bsb.6:31: For the entrance to the inner sanctuary, Solomon constructed doors of olive wood with five-sided doorposts.
bsb.6:32: The double doors were made of olive wood, and he carved into them cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers and overlaid the cherubim and palm trees with hammered gold.
bsb.6:33: In the same way he made four-sided doorposts of olive wood for the sanctuary entrance.
bsb.6:34: The two doors were made of cypress wood, and each had two folding panels.
bsb.6:35: He carved into them cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers; and he overlaid them with gold, hammered evenly over the carvings.
bsb.6:36: Solomon built the inner courtyard with three rows of dressed stone and one row of trimmed cedar beams.
bsb.6:37: The foundation of the house of the LORD was laid in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign, in the month of Ziv.
bsb.6:38: In his eleventh year and eighth month, the month of Bul, the temple was finished in every detail and according to every specification. So he built the temple in seven years.
bsb.7:1: Solomon, however, took thirteen years to complete the construction of his entire palace.
bsb.7:2: He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon a hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high, with four rows of cedar pillars supporting the cedar beams.
bsb.7:3: The house was roofed with cedar above the beams that rested on the pillars—forty-five beams, fifteen per row.
bsb.7:4: There were three rows of high windows facing one another in three tiers.
bsb.7:5: All the doorways had rectangular frames, with the openings facing one another in three tiers.
bsb.7:6: Solomon made his colonnade fifty cubits long and thirty cubits wide, with a portico in front of it and a canopy with pillars in front of the portico.
bsb.7:7: In addition, he built a hall for the throne, the Hall of Justice, where he was to judge. It was paneled with cedar from floor to ceiling.
bsb.7:8: And the palace where Solomon would live, set further back, was of similar construction. He also made a palace like this hall for Pharaoh’s daughter, whom he had married.
bsb.7:9: All these buildings were constructed with costly stones, cut to size and trimmed with saws inside and out from the foundation to the eaves, and from the outside to the great courtyard.
bsb.7:10: The foundations were laid with large, costly stones, some ten cubits long and some eight cubits long.
bsb.7:11: Above these were high-grade stones, cut to size, and cedar beams.
bsb.7:12: The great courtyard was surrounded by three rows of dressed stone and a row of trimmed cedar beams, as were the inner courtyard and portico of the house of the LORD.
bsb.7:13: Now King Solomon sent to bring Huram from Tyre.
bsb.7:14: He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a craftsman in bronze. Huram had great skill, understanding, and knowledge for every kind of bronze work. So he came to King Solomon and carried out all his work.
bsb.7:15: He cast two pillars of bronze, each eighteen cubits high and twelve cubits in circumference.
bsb.7:16: He also made two capitals of cast bronze to set on top of the pillars, each capital five cubits high.
bsb.7:17: For the capitals on top of the pillars he made a network of lattice, with wreaths of chainwork, seven for each capital.
bsb.7:18: Likewise, he made the pillars with two rows of pomegranates around each grating to cover each capital atop the pillars.
bsb.7:19: And the capitals atop the pillars in the portico were shaped like lilies, four cubits high.
bsb.7:20: On the capitals of both pillars, just above the rounded projection next to the network, were the two hundred pomegranates in rows encircling each capital.
bsb.7:21: Thus he set up the pillars at the portico of the temple. The pillar to the south he named Jachin, and the pillar to the north he named Boaz.
bsb.7:22: And the tops of the pillars were shaped like lilies. So the work of the pillars was completed.
bsb.7:23: He also made the Sea of cast metal. It was circular in shape, measuring ten cubits from rim to rim, five cubits in height, and thirty cubits in circumference.
bsb.7:24: Below the rim, ornamental buds encircled it, ten per cubit all the way around the Sea, cast in two rows as a part of the Sea.
bsb.7:25: The Sea stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The Sea rested on them, with all their hindquarters toward the center.
bsb.7:26: It was a handbreadth thick, and its rim was fashioned like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It could hold two thousand baths.
bsb.7:27: In addition, he made ten movable stands of bronze, each four cubits long, four cubits wide, and three cubits high.
bsb.7:28: This was the design of the stands: They had side panels attached to uprights,
bsb.7:29: and on the panels between the uprights were lions, oxen, and cherubim. On the uprights was a pedestal above, and below the lions and oxen were wreaths of beveled work.
bsb.7:30: Each stand had four bronze wheels with bronze axles and a basin resting on four supports, with wreaths at each side.
bsb.7:31: The opening to each stand inside the crown at the top was one cubit deep, with a round opening like the design of a pedestal, a cubit and a half wide. And around its opening were engravings, but the panels of the stands were square, not round.
bsb.7:32: There were four wheels under the panels, and the axles of the wheels were attached to the stand; each wheel was a cubit and a half in diameter.
bsb.7:33: The wheels were made like chariot wheels; their axles, rims, spokes, and hubs were all of cast metal.
bsb.7:34: Each stand had four handles, one for each corner, projecting from the stand.
bsb.7:35: At the top of each stand was a circular band half a cubit high. The supports and panels were cast as a unit with the top of the stand.
bsb.7:36: He engraved cherubim, lions, and palm trees on the surfaces of the supports and panels, wherever each had space, with wreaths all around.
bsb.7:37: In this way he made the ten stands, each with the same casting, dimensions, and shape.
bsb.7:38: He also made ten bronze basins, each holding forty baths and measuring four cubits across, one basin for each of the ten stands.
bsb.7:39: He set five stands on the south side of the temple and five on the north, and he put the Sea on the south side, at the southeast corner of the temple.
bsb.7:40: Additionally, Huram made the pots, shovels, and sprinkling bowls. So Huram finished all the work that he had undertaken for King Solomon in the house of the LORD:
bsb.7:41: the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals atop the pillars; the two sets of network covering both bowls of the capitals atop the pillars;
bsb.7:42: the four hundred pomegranates for the two sets of network (two rows of pomegranates for each network covering both the bowl-shaped capitals atop the pillars);
bsb.7:43: the ten stands; the ten basins on the stands;
bsb.7:44: the Sea; the twelve oxen underneath the Sea;
bsb.7:45: and the pots, shovels, and sprinkling bowls. All the articles that Huram made for King Solomon in the house of the LORD were made of burnished bronze.
bsb.7:46: The king had them cast in clay molds in the plain of the Jordan between Succoth and Zarethan.
bsb.7:47: Solomon left all these articles unweighed, because there were so many. The weight of the bronze could not be determined.
bsb.7:48: Solomon also made all the furnishings for the house of the LORD: the golden altar; the golden table on which was placed the Bread of the Presence;
bsb.7:49: the lampstands of pure gold in front of the inner sanctuary, five on the right side and five on the left; the gold flowers, lamps, and tongs;
bsb.7:50: the pure gold basins, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, ladles, and censers; and the gold hinges for the doors of the inner temple (that is, the Most Holy Place) as well as for the doors of the main hall of the temple.
bsb.7:51: So all the work that King Solomon had performed for the house of the LORD was completed. Then Solomon brought in the items his father David had dedicated—the silver, the gold, and the furnishings—and he placed them in the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
bsb.8:1: At that time Solomon assembled before him in Jerusalem the elders of Israel—all the tribal heads and family leaders of the Israelites—to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Zion, the City of David.
bsb.8:2: And all the men of Israel came together to King Solomon at the feast in the seventh month, the month of Ethanim.
bsb.8:3: When all the elders of Israel had arrived, the priests took up the ark,
bsb.8:4: and they brought up the ark of the LORD and the Tent of Meeting with all its sacred furnishings. So the priests and Levites carried them up.
bsb.8:5: There, before the ark, King Solomon and the whole congregation of Israel who had assembled with him sacrificed so many sheep and oxen that they could not be counted or numbered.
bsb.8:6: Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place in the inner sanctuary of the temple, the Most Holy Place, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
bsb.8:7: For the cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark and overshadowed the ark and its poles.
bsb.8:8: The poles extended far enough that their ends were visible from the Holy Place in front of the inner sanctuary, but not from outside the Holy Place; and they are there to this day.
bsb.8:9: There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses had placed in it at Horeb, where the LORD had made a covenant with the Israelites after they had come out of the land of Egypt.
bsb.8:10: And when the priests came out of the Holy Place, the cloud filled the house of the LORD
bsb.8:11: so that the priests could not stand there to minister because of the cloud; for the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.
bsb.8:12: Then Solomon declared: “The LORD has said that He would dwell in the thick cloud.
bsb.8:13: I have indeed built You an exalted house, a place for You to dwell forever.”
bsb.8:14: And as the whole assembly of Israel stood there, the king turned around and blessed them all
bsb.8:15: and said: “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who has fulfilled with His own hand what He spoke with His mouth to my father David, saying,
bsb.8:16: ‘Since the day I brought My people Israel out of Egypt, I have not chosen a city from any tribe of Israel in which to build a house so that My Name would be there. But I have chosen David to be over My people Israel.’
bsb.8:17: Now it was in the heart of my father David to build a house for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
bsb.8:18: But the LORD said to my father David, ‘Since it was in your heart to build a house for My Name, you have done well to have this in your heart.
bsb.8:19: Nevertheless, you are not the one to build it; but your son, your own offspring, will build the house for My Name.’
bsb.8:20: Now the LORD has fulfilled the word that He spoke. I have succeeded my father David, and I sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD promised. I have built the house for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
bsb.8:21: And there I have provided a place for the ark, which contains the covenant of the LORD that He made with our fathers when He brought them out of the land of Egypt.”
bsb.8:22: Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in front of the whole assembly of Israel, spread out his hands toward heaven,
bsb.8:23: and said: “O LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like You in heaven above or on earth below, keeping Your covenant of loving devotion with Your servants who walk before You with all their hearts.
bsb.8:24: You have kept Your promise to Your servant, my father David. What You spoke with Your mouth You have fulfilled with Your hand this day.
bsb.8:25: Therefore now, O LORD, God of Israel, keep for Your servant, my father David, what You promised when You said: ‘You will never fail to have a man to sit before Me on the throne of Israel, if only your descendants guard their way to walk before Me as you have done.’
bsb.8:26: And now, O God of Israel, please confirm what You promised to Your servant, my father David.
bsb.8:27: But will God indeed dwell upon the earth? Even heaven, the highest heaven, cannot contain You, much less this temple I have built.
bsb.8:28: Yet regard the prayer and plea of Your servant, O LORD my God, so that You may hear the cry and the prayer that Your servant is praying before You today.
bsb.8:29: May Your eyes be open toward this temple night and day, toward the place of which You said, ‘My Name shall be there,’ so that You may hear the prayer that Your servant prays toward this place.
bsb.8:30: Hear the plea of Your servant and of Your people Israel when they pray toward this place. May You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place. May You hear and forgive.
bsb.8:31: When a man sins against his neighbor and is required to take an oath, and he comes to take an oath before Your altar in this temple,
bsb.8:32: then may You hear from heaven and act. May You judge Your servants, condemning the wicked man by bringing down on his own head what he has done, and justifying the righteous man by rewarding him according to his righteousness.
bsb.8:33: When Your people Israel are defeated before an enemy because they have sinned against You, and they return to You and confess Your name, praying and pleading with You in this temple,
bsb.8:34: then may You hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your people Israel. May You restore them to the land You gave to their fathers.
bsb.8:35: When the skies are shut and there is no rain because Your people have sinned against You, and they pray toward this place and confess Your name, and they turn from their sins because You have afflicted them,
bsb.8:36: then may You hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your servants, Your people Israel, so that You may teach them the good way in which they should walk. May You send rain on the land that You gave Your people as an inheritance.
bsb.8:37: When famine or plague comes upon the land, or blight or mildew or locusts or grasshoppers, or when their enemy besieges them in their cities, whatever plague or sickness may come,
bsb.8:38: then may whatever prayer or petition Your people Israel make—each knowing his own afflictions and spreading out his hands toward this temple—
bsb.8:39: be heard by You from heaven, Your dwelling place. And may You forgive and act, and repay each man according to all his ways, since You know his heart—for You alone know the hearts of all men—
bsb.8:40: so that they may fear You all the days they live in the land that You gave to our fathers.
bsb.8:41: And as for the foreigner who is not of Your people Israel but has come from a distant land because of Your name—
bsb.8:42: for they will hear of Your great name and mighty hand and outstretched arm—when he comes and prays toward this temple,
bsb.8:43: then may You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place, and do according to all for which the foreigner calls to You. Then all the peoples of the earth will know Your name and fear You, as do Your people Israel, and they will know that this house I have built is called by Your Name.
bsb.8:44: When Your people go to war against their enemies, wherever You send them, and when they pray to the LORD in the direction of the city You have chosen and the house I have built for Your Name,
bsb.8:45: then may You hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and may You uphold their cause.
bsb.8:46: When they sin against You—for there is no one who does not sin—and You become angry with them and deliver them to an enemy who takes them as captives to his own land, whether far or near,
bsb.8:47: and when they come to their senses in the land to which they were taken, and they repent and plead with You in the land of their captors, saying, ‘We have sinned and done wrong; we have acted wickedly,’
bsb.8:48: and when they return to You with all their heart and soul in the land of the enemies who took them captive, and when they pray to You in the direction of the land that You gave to their fathers, the city You have chosen, and the house I have built for Your Name,
bsb.8:49: then may You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place, their prayer and petition, and may You uphold their cause.
bsb.8:50: May You forgive Your people who have sinned against You and all the transgressions they have committed against You, and may You grant them compassion in the eyes of their captors to show them mercy.
bsb.8:51: For they are Your people and Your inheritance; You brought them out of Egypt, out of the furnace for iron.
bsb.8:52: May Your eyes be open to the pleas of Your servant and of Your people Israel, and may You listen to them whenever they call to You.
bsb.8:53: For You, O Lord GOD, as Your inheritance, have set them apart from all the peoples of the earth, as You spoke through Your servant Moses when You brought our fathers out of Egypt.”
bsb.8:54: Now when Solomon had finished praying this entire prayer and petition to the LORD, he got up before the altar of the LORD, where he had been kneeling with his hands spread out toward heaven.
bsb.8:55: And he stood and blessed the whole assembly of Israel in a loud voice, saying:
bsb.8:56: “Blessed be the LORD, who has given rest to His people Israel according to all that He promised. Not one word has failed of all the good promises He made through His servant Moses.
bsb.8:57: May the LORD our God be with us, as He was with our fathers. May He never leave us nor forsake us.
bsb.8:58: May He incline our hearts to Himself, to walk in all His ways and to keep the commandments and statutes and ordinances He commanded our fathers.
bsb.8:59: And may these words with which I have made my petition before the LORD be near to the LORD our God day and night, so that He may uphold the cause of His servant and of His people Israel as each day requires,
bsb.8:60: so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD is God. There is no other!
bsb.8:61: So let your heart be fully devoted to the LORD our God, as it is this day, to walk in His statutes and to keep His commandments.”
bsb.8:62: Then the king and all Israel with him offered sacrifices before the LORD.
bsb.8:63: And Solomon offered as peace offerings to the LORD 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep. So the king and all the Israelites dedicated the house of the LORD.
bsb.8:64: On that same day the king consecrated the middle of the courtyard in front of the house of the LORD, and there he offered the burnt offerings, the grain offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings, since the bronze altar before the LORD was too small to contain all these offerings.
bsb.8:65: So at that time Solomon and all Israel with him—a great assembly of people from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt—kept the feast before the LORD our God for seven days and seven more days—fourteen days in all.
bsb.8:66: On the fifteenth day Solomon sent the people away. So they blessed the king and went home, joyful and glad in heart for all the good things that the LORD had done for His servant David and for His people Israel.
bsb.9:1: Now when Solomon had finished building the house of the LORD and the royal palace, and had achieved all that he had desired to do,
bsb.9:2: the LORD appeared to him a second time, as He had appeared to him at Gibeon.
bsb.9:3: And the LORD said to him: “I have heard your prayer and petition before Me. I have consecrated this temple you have built by putting My Name there forever; My eyes and My heart will be there for all time.
bsb.9:4: And as for you, if you walk before Me as your father David walked, with a heart of integrity and uprightness, doing all I have commanded you, and if you keep My statutes and ordinances,
bsb.9:5: then I will establish your royal throne over Israel forever, as I promised your father David when I said, ‘You will never fail to have a man on the throne of Israel.’
bsb.9:6: But if indeed you or your sons turn away from following Me and do not keep the commandments and statutes I have set before you, and if you go off to serve and worship other gods,
bsb.9:7: then I will cut off Israel from the land that I have given them, and I will banish from My presence this temple I have sanctified for My Name. Then Israel will become an object of scorn and ridicule among all peoples.
bsb.9:8: And when this temple has become a heap of rubble, all who pass by it will be appalled and will hiss and say, ‘Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?’
bsb.9:9: And others will answer, ‘Because they have forsaken the LORD their God who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and have embraced other gods, worshiping and serving them—because of this, the LORD has brought all this disaster upon them.’”
bsb.9:10: Now at the end of the twenty years during which Solomon built these two houses, the house of the LORD and the royal palace,
bsb.9:11: King Solomon gave twenty towns in the land of Galilee to Hiram king of Tyre, who had supplied him with cedar and cypress logs and gold for his every desire.
bsb.9:12: So Hiram went out from Tyre to inspect the towns that Solomon had given him, but he was not pleased with them.
bsb.9:13: “What are these towns you have given me, my brother?” asked Hiram, and he called them the Land of Cabul, as they are called to this day.
bsb.9:14: And Hiram had sent the king 120 talents of gold.
bsb.9:15: This is the account of the forced labor that King Solomon imposed to build the house of the LORD, his own palace, the supporting terraces, and the wall of Jerusalem, as well as Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
bsb.9:16: Pharaoh king of Egypt had attacked and captured Gezer. He had set it on fire, killed the Canaanites who lived in the city, and given it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon’s wife.
bsb.9:17: So Solomon rebuilt Gezer, Lower Beth-horon,
bsb.9:18: Baalath, and Tamar in the Wilderness of Judah,
bsb.9:19: as well as all the store cities that Solomon had for his chariots and horses—whatever he desired to build in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and throughout the land of his dominion.
bsb.9:20: As for all the people who remained of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites (the people who were not Israelites)—
bsb.9:21: their descendants who remained in the land, those whom the Israelites were unable to devote to destruction—Solomon conscripted these people to be forced laborers, as they are to this day.
bsb.9:22: But Solomon did not consign any of the Israelites to slavery, because they were his men of war, his servants, his officers, his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry.
bsb.9:23: They were also the chief officers over Solomon’s projects: 550 supervisors over the people who did the work.
bsb.9:24: As soon as Pharaoh’s daughter had come up from the City of David to the palace that Solomon had built for her, he built the supporting terraces.
bsb.9:25: Three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar he had built for the LORD, burning incense with them before the LORD. So he completed the temple.
bsb.9:26: King Solomon also assembled a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber, which is near Eloth in Edom, on the shore of the Red Sea.
bsb.9:27: And Hiram sent his servants, men who knew the sea, to serve in the fleet with Solomon’s servants.
bsb.9:28: They sailed to Ophir and imported gold from there—420 talents—and delivered it to Solomon.
bsb.10:1: Now when the queen of Sheba heard about the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, she came to test him with difficult questions.
bsb.10:2: She arrived in Jerusalem with a very large caravan—with camels bearing spices, gold in great abundance, and precious stones. So she came to Solomon and spoke to him all that was on her mind.
bsb.10:3: And Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was too difficult for the king to explain.
bsb.10:4: When the queen of Sheba saw all the wisdom of Solomon, the palace he had built,
bsb.10:5: the food at his table, the seating of his servants, the service and attire of his attendants and cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he presented at the house of the LORD, it took her breath away.
bsb.10:6: She said to the king, “The report I heard in my own country about your words and wisdom is true.
bsb.10:7: But I did not believe these things until I came and saw with my own eyes. Indeed, not even half was told to me. Your wisdom and prosperity have far exceeded the report I heard.
bsb.10:8: How blessed are your men! How blessed are these servants of yours who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!
bsb.10:9: Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you to set you on the throne of Israel. Because of the LORD’s eternal love for Israel, He has made you king to carry out justice and righteousness.”
bsb.10:10: Then she gave the king 120 talents of gold, a great quantity of spices, and precious stones. Never again was such an abundance of spices brought in as those the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
bsb.10:11: (The fleet of Hiram that brought gold from Ophir also brought from Ophir a great cargo of almug wood and precious stones.
bsb.10:12: The king made the almug wood into steps for the house of the LORD and for the king’s palace, and into lyres and harps for the singers. Never before had such almug wood been brought in, nor has such been seen to this day.)
bsb.10:13: King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all she desired—whatever she asked—besides what he had given her out of his royal bounty. Then she left and returned to her own country, along with her servants.
bsb.10:14: The weight of gold that came to Solomon each year was 666 talents,
bsb.10:15: not including the revenue from the merchants, traders, and all the Arabian kings and governors of the land.
bsb.10:16: King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold; six hundred shekels of gold went into each shield.
bsb.10:17: He also made three hundred small shields of hammered gold; three minas of gold went into each shield. And the king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
bsb.10:18: Additionally, the king made a great throne of ivory and overlaid it with pure gold.
bsb.10:19: The throne had six steps, and its back had a rounded top. There were armrests on both sides of the seat, with a lion standing beside each armrest.
bsb.10:20: Twelve lions stood on the six steps, one at either end of each step. Nothing like this had ever been made for any kingdom.
bsb.10:21: All King Solomon’s drinking cups were gold, and all the utensils of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. There was no silver, because it was accounted as nothing in the days of Solomon.
bsb.10:22: For the king had the ships of Tarshish at sea with Hiram’s fleet, and once every three years the ships of Tarshish would arrive bearing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
bsb.10:23: So King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.
bsb.10:24: The whole world sought an audience with Solomon to hear the wisdom that God had put in his heart.
bsb.10:25: Year after year, each visitor would bring his tribute: articles of silver and gold, clothing, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.
bsb.10:26: Solomon accumulated 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses, which he stationed in the chariot cities and also with him in Jerusalem.
bsb.10:27: The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as abundant as sycamore in the foothills.
bsb.10:28: Solomon’s horses were imported from Egypt and Kue; the royal merchants purchased them from Kue.
bsb.10:29: A chariot could be imported from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty. Likewise, they exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Aram.
bsb.11:1: King Solomon, however, loved many foreign women along with the daughter of Pharaoh—women of Moab, Ammon, Edom, and Sidon, as well as Hittite women.
bsb.11:2: These women were from the nations about which the LORD had told the Israelites, “You must not intermarry with them, for surely they will turn your hearts after their gods.” Yet Solomon clung to these women in love.
bsb.11:3: He had seven hundred wives of royal birth and three hundred concubines—and his wives turned his heart away.
bsb.11:4: For when Solomon grew old, his wives turned his heart after other gods, and he was not wholeheartedly devoted to the LORD his God, as his father David had been.
bsb.11:5: Solomon followed Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians and Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.
bsb.11:6: So Solomon did evil in the sight of the LORD; unlike his father David, he did not follow the LORD completely.
bsb.11:7: At that time on a hill east of Jerusalem, Solomon built a high place for Chemosh the abomination of Moab and for Molech the abomination of the Ammonites.
bsb.11:8: He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and sacrificed to their gods.
bsb.11:9: Now the LORD grew angry with Solomon, because his heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice.
bsb.11:10: Although He had warned Solomon explicitly not to follow other gods, Solomon did not keep the LORD’s command.
bsb.11:11: Then the LORD said to Solomon, “Because you have done this and have not kept My covenant and My statutes, which I have commanded you, I will tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant.
bsb.11:12: Nevertheless, for the sake of your father David, I will not do it during your lifetime; I will tear it out of the hand of your son.
bsb.11:13: Yet I will not tear the whole kingdom away from him. I will give one tribe to your son for the sake of My servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen.”
bsb.11:14: Then the LORD raised up against Solomon an adversary, Hadad the Edomite, from the royal line of Edom.
bsb.11:15: Earlier, when David was in Edom, Joab the commander of the army had gone to bury the dead and had struck down every male in Edom.
bsb.11:16: Joab and all Israel had stayed there six months, until he had killed every male in Edom.
bsb.11:17: But Hadad, still just a young boy, had fled to Egypt, along with some Edomites who were servants of his father.
bsb.11:18: Hadad and his men set out from Midian and went to Paran. They took men from Paran with them and went to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave Hadad a house and land and provided him with food.
bsb.11:19: There Hadad found such great favor in the sight of Pharaoh that he gave to him in marriage the sister of Queen Tahpenes, his own wife.
bsb.11:20: And the sister of Tahpenes bore Hadad a son named Genubath. Tahpenes herself weaned him in Pharaoh’s palace, and Genubath lived there among the sons of Pharaoh.
bsb.11:21: When Hadad heard in Egypt that David had rested with his fathers and that Joab, the commander of the army, was dead, he said to Pharaoh, “Let me go, that I may return to my own country.”
bsb.11:22: But Pharaoh asked him, “What have you lacked here with me that you suddenly want to go back to your own country?” “Nothing,” Hadad replied, “but please let me go.”
bsb.11:23: And God raised up against Solomon another adversary, Rezon the son of Eliada, who had fled from his master, Hadadezer king of Zobah,
bsb.11:24: and had gathered men to himself. When David killed the Zobaites, Rezon captained a band of raiders and went to Damascus, where they settled and gained control.
bsb.11:25: Rezon was Israel’s enemy throughout the days of Solomon, adding to the trouble caused by Hadad. So Rezon ruled over Aram with hostility toward Israel.
bsb.11:26: Now Jeroboam son of Nebat was an Ephraimite from Zeredah whose mother was a widow named Zeruah. Jeroboam was a servant of Solomon, but he rebelled against the king,
bsb.11:27: and this is the account of his rebellion against the king. Solomon had built the supporting terraces and repaired the gap in the wall of the city of his father David.
bsb.11:28: Now Jeroboam was a mighty man of valor. So when Solomon noticed that the young man was industrious, he put him in charge of the whole labor force of the house of Joseph.
bsb.11:29: During that time, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met Jeroboam on the road as he was going out of Jerusalem. Now Ahijah had wrapped himself in a new cloak, and the two of them were alone in the open field.
bsb.11:30: And Ahijah took hold of the new cloak he was wearing, tore it into twelve pieces,
bsb.11:31: and said to Jeroboam, “Take ten pieces for yourself, for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Behold, I will tear the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and I will give you ten tribes.
bsb.11:32: But one tribe will remain for the sake of My servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel.
bsb.11:33: For they have forsaken Me to worship Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the Ammonites. They have not walked in My ways, nor done what is right in My eyes, nor kept My statutes and judgments, as Solomon’s father David did.
bsb.11:34: Nevertheless, I will not take the whole kingdom out of Solomon’s hand, because I have made him ruler all the days of his life for the sake of David My servant, whom I chose because he kept My commandments and statutes.
bsb.11:35: But I will take ten tribes of the kingdom from the hand of his son and give them to you.
bsb.11:36: I will give one tribe to his son, so that My servant David will always have a lamp before Me in Jerusalem, the city where I chose to put My Name.
bsb.11:37: But as for you, I will take you, and you shall reign over all that your heart desires, and you will be king over Israel.
bsb.11:38: If you listen to all that I command you, walk in My ways, and do what is right in My sight in order to keep My statutes and commandments as My servant David did, then I will be with you. I will build you a lasting dynasty just as I built for David, and I will give Israel to you.
bsb.11:39: Because of this, I will humble David’s descendants—but not forever.’”
bsb.11:40: Solomon therefore sought to kill Jeroboam. But Jeroboam arose and fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, where he remained until the death of Solomon.
bsb.11:41: As for the rest of the acts of Solomon—all that he did, as well as his wisdom—are they not written in the Book of the Acts of Solomon?
bsb.11:42: Thus the time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.
bsb.11:43: And Solomon rested with his fathers and was buried in the city of his father David. And his son Rehoboam reigned in his place.
bsb.12:1: Then Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had gone there to make him king.
bsb.12:2: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard about this, he was still in Egypt where he had fled from King Solomon and had been living ever since.
bsb.12:3: So they sent for Jeroboam, and he and the whole assembly of Israel came to Rehoboam and said,
bsb.12:4: “Your father put a heavy yoke on us. But now you should lighten the burden of your father’s service and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we will serve you.”
bsb.12:5: Rehoboam answered, “Go away for three days and then return to me.” So the people departed.
bsb.12:6: Then King Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime. “How do you advise me to respond to these people?” he asked.
bsb.12:7: They replied, “If you will be a servant to these people and serve them this day, and if you will respond by speaking kind words to them, they will be your servants forever.”
bsb.12:8: But Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders; instead, he consulted the young men who had grown up with him and served him.
bsb.12:9: He asked them, “What message do you advise that we send back to these people who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Lighten the yoke your father put on us’?”
bsb.12:10: The young men who had grown up with him replied, “This is how you should answer these people who said to you, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you should make it lighter.’ This is what you should tell them: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!
bsb.12:11: Whereas my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.’”
bsb.12:12: After three days, Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam, since the king had said, “Come back to me on the third day.”
bsb.12:13: And the king answered the people harshly. He rejected the advice of the elders
bsb.12:14: and spoke to them as the young men had advised, saying, “Whereas my father made your yoke heavy, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.”
bsb.12:15: So the king did not listen to the people, and indeed this turn of events was from the LORD, to fulfill the word He had spoken to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah the Shilonite.
bsb.12:16: When all Israel saw that the king had refused to listen to them, they answered the king: “What portion do we have in David, and what inheritance in the son of Jesse? To your tents, O Israel! Look now to your own house, O David!” So the Israelites went home,
bsb.12:17: but Rehoboam still reigned over the Israelites living in the cities of Judah.
bsb.12:18: Then King Rehoboam sent out Adoram, who was in charge of the forced labor, but all Israel stoned him to death. And King Rehoboam mounted his chariot in haste and escaped to Jerusalem.
bsb.12:19: So to this day Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David.
bsb.12:20: When all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, they summoned him to the assembly and made him king over all Israel. Only the tribe of Judah followed the house of David.
bsb.12:21: And when Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he mobilized the whole house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin—180,000 chosen warriors—to fight against the house of Israel and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam son of Solomon.
bsb.12:22: But the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God:
bsb.12:23: “Tell Rehoboam son of Solomon king of Judah, all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and the rest of the people
bsb.12:24: that this is what the LORD says: ‘You are not to go up and fight against your brothers, the Israelites. Each of you must return home, for this word is from Me.’” So they listened to the word of the LORD and turned back according to the word of the LORD.
bsb.12:25: Then Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there. And from there he went out and built Penuel.
bsb.12:26: Jeroboam said in his heart, “Now the kingdom might revert to the house of David.
bsb.12:27: If these people go up to offer sacrifices in the house of the LORD at Jerusalem, their hearts will return to their lord, Rehoboam king of Judah; then they will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah.”
bsb.12:28: After seeking advice, the king made two golden calves and said to the people, “Going up to Jerusalem is too much for you. Here, O Israel, are your gods, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.”
bsb.12:29: One calf he set up in Bethel, and the other in Dan.
bsb.12:30: And this thing became a sin; the people walked as far as Dan to worship before one of the calves.
bsb.12:31: Jeroboam also built shrines on the high places and appointed from every class of people priests who were not Levites.
bsb.12:32: And Jeroboam ordained a feast on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, like the feast that was in Judah, and he offered sacrifices on the altar; he made this offering in Bethel to sacrifice to the calves he had set up, and he installed priests in Bethel for the high places he had set up.
bsb.12:33: On the fifteenth day of the eighth month, a month of his own choosing, Jeroboam offered sacrifices on the altar he had set up in Bethel. So he ordained a feast for the Israelites, offered sacrifices on the altar, and burned incense.
bsb.13:1: Suddenly, as Jeroboam was standing beside the altar to burn incense, there came a man of God from Judah to Bethel by the word of the LORD.
bsb.13:2: And he cried out against the altar by the word of the LORD, “O altar, O altar, this is what the LORD says: ‘A son named Josiah will be born to the house of David, and upon you he will sacrifice the priests of the high places who burn incense upon you, and human bones will be burned upon you.’”
bsb.13:3: That day the man of God gave a sign, saying, “The LORD has spoken this sign: ‘Surely the altar will be split apart, and the ashes upon it will be poured out.’”
bsb.13:4: Now when King Jeroboam, who was at the altar in Bethel, heard the word that the man of God had cried out against it, he stretched out his hand and said, “Seize him!” But the hand he stretched out toward him withered, so that he could not pull it back.
bsb.13:5: And the altar was split apart, and the ashes poured out, according to the sign that the man of God had given by the word of the LORD.
bsb.13:6: Then the king responded to the man of God, “Intercede with the LORD your God and pray that my hand may be restored.” So the man of God interceded with the LORD, and the king’s hand was restored to him as it was before.
bsb.13:7: Then the king said to the man of God, “Come home with me and refresh yourself, and I will give you a reward.”
bsb.13:8: But the man of God replied, “If you were to give me half your possessions, I still would not go with you, nor would I eat bread or drink water in this place.
bsb.13:9: For this is what I was commanded by the word of the LORD: ‘You must not eat bread or drink water or return by the way you came.’”
bsb.13:10: So the man of God went another way and did not return by the way he had come to Bethel.
bsb.13:11: Now a certain old prophet was living in Bethel, and his sons came and told him all the deeds that the man of God had done that day in Bethel. They also told their father the words that the man had spoken to the king.
bsb.13:12: “Which way did he go?” their father asked. And his sons showed him the way taken by the man of God, who had come from Judah.
bsb.13:13: So the prophet said to his sons, “Saddle the donkey for me.” Then they saddled the donkey for him, and he mounted it
bsb.13:14: and went after the man of God. He found him sitting under an oak tree and asked, “Are you the man of God who came from Judah?” “I am,” he replied.
bsb.13:15: So the prophet said to the man of God, “Come home with me and eat some bread.”
bsb.13:16: But the man replied, “I cannot return with you or eat bread or drink water with you in this place.
bsb.13:17: For I have been told by the word of the LORD: ‘You must not eat bread or drink water there or return by the way you came.’”
bsb.13:18: Then the prophet replied, “I too am a prophet like you, and an angel spoke to me by the word of the LORD, saying, ‘Bring him back with you to your house, so that he may eat bread and drink water.’” The old prophet was lying to him,
bsb.13:19: but the man of God went back with him, ate bread in his house, and drank water.
bsb.13:20: While they were sitting at the table, the word of the LORD came to the prophet who had brought him back,
bsb.13:21: and the prophet cried out to the man of God who had come from Judah, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Because you have defied the word of the LORD and have not kept the commandment that the LORD your God gave you,
bsb.13:22: but you went back and ate bread and drank water in the place where He told you not to do so, your body shall never reach the tomb of your fathers.’”
bsb.13:23: And after the man of God had finished eating and drinking, the old prophet who had brought him back saddled the donkey for him.
bsb.13:24: As he went on his way, a lion met him on the road and killed him, and his body was left lying in the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside it.
bsb.13:25: And there were men passing by who saw the body lying in the road with the lion standing beside it, and they went and reported this in the city where the old prophet lived.
bsb.13:26: When the prophet who had brought him back from his journey heard this, he said, “It is the man of God who disobeyed the command of the LORD. Therefore the LORD has delivered him to the lion, and it has mauled him and killed him, according to the word that the LORD had spoken to him.”
bsb.13:27: Then the old prophet instructed his sons, “Saddle the donkey for me.” So they saddled it,
bsb.13:28: and he went and found the body lying in the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside it. The lion had not eaten the body or mauled the donkey.
bsb.13:29: So the old prophet lifted up the body of the man of God, laid it on the donkey, and brought it back to his own city to mourn for him and bury him.
bsb.13:30: Then he laid the body in his own tomb, and they lamented over him, “Oh, my brother!”
bsb.13:31: After he had buried him, the prophet said to his sons, “When I die, you must bury me in the tomb where the man of God is buried. Lay my bones beside his bones,
bsb.13:32: for the message that he cried out by the word of the LORD against the altar in Bethel and against all the shrines on the high places in the cities of Samaria will surely come to pass.”
bsb.13:33: Even after these events, Jeroboam did not repent of his evil ways, but again he appointed priests for the high places from every class of people. He ordained anyone who desired to be a priest of the high places.
bsb.13:34: And this was the sin of the house of Jeroboam that led to its extermination and destruction from the face of the earth.
bsb.14:1: At that time Abijah son of Jeroboam became ill,
bsb.14:2: and Jeroboam said to his wife, “Now get up, disguise yourself so they will not recognize you as my wife, and go to Shiloh. For Ahijah the prophet is there; it was he who spoke about my kingship over this people.
bsb.14:3: Take with you ten loaves of bread, some cakes, and a jar of honey, and go to him. He will tell you what will become of the boy.”
bsb.14:4: Jeroboam’s wife did as instructed; she arose and went to Shiloh and arrived at Ahijah’s house. Now Ahijah could not see, for his eyes were dim because of his age.
bsb.14:5: But the LORD had said to Ahijah, “Behold, the wife of Jeroboam is coming to ask you about her son, for he is ill. You are to say such and such to her, because when she arrives, she will be disguised.”
bsb.14:6: So when Ahijah heard the sound of her feet entering the door, he said, “Come in, wife of Jeroboam! Why are you disguised? For I have been sent to you with bad news.
bsb.14:7: Go, tell Jeroboam that this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I raised you up from among the people and appointed you ruler over My people Israel.
bsb.14:8: I tore the kingdom away from the house of David and gave it to you. But you were not like My servant David, who kept My commandments and followed Me with all his heart, doing only what was right in My eyes.
bsb.14:9: You have done more evil than all who came before you. You have proceeded to make for yourself other gods and molten images to provoke Me, and you have flung Me behind your back.
bsb.14:10: Because of all this, behold, I am bringing disaster on the house of Jeroboam: I will cut off from Jeroboam every male, both slave and free, in Israel; I will burn up the house of Jeroboam as one burns up dung until it is gone!
bsb.14:11: Anyone belonging to Jeroboam who dies in the city will be eaten by dogs, and anyone who dies in the field will be eaten by the birds of the air.’ For the LORD has spoken.
bsb.14:12: As for you, get up and go home. When your feet enter the city, the child will die.
bsb.14:13: All Israel will mourn for him and bury him. For this is the only one belonging to Jeroboam who will receive a proper burial, because only in him has the LORD, the God of Israel, found any good in the house of Jeroboam.
bsb.14:14: Moreover, the LORD will raise up for Himself a king over Israel who will cut off the house of Jeroboam. This is the day—yes, even today!
bsb.14:15: For the LORD will strike Israel as a reed is shaken in the water. He will uproot Israel from this good land that He gave their fathers, and He will scatter them beyond the Euphrates, because they have made their Asherah poles, provoking the LORD to anger.
bsb.14:16: So He will give Israel over on account of the sins Jeroboam has committed and has caused Israel to commit.”
bsb.14:17: Then Jeroboam’s wife got up and departed for Tirzah, and as soon as she stepped over the threshold of the house, the boy died.
bsb.14:18: And they buried him, and all Israel mourned for him, according to the word that the LORD had spoken through His servant Ahijah the prophet.
bsb.14:19: As for the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he waged war and how he reigned, they are indeed written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
bsb.14:20: And the length of Jeroboam’s reign was twenty-two years, and he rested with his fathers, and his son Nadab reigned in his place.
bsb.14:21: Meanwhile, Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned in Judah. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen from all the tribes of Israel in which to put His Name. His mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonite.
bsb.14:22: And Judah did evil in the sight of the LORD, and by the sins they committed they provoked Him to jealous anger more than all their fathers had done.
bsb.14:23: They also built for themselves high places, sacred pillars, and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.
bsb.14:24: There were even male shrine prostitutes in the land. They imitated all the abominations of the nations the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.
bsb.14:25: In the fifth year of Rehoboam’s reign, Shishak king of Egypt came up and attacked Jerusalem.
bsb.14:26: He seized the treasures of the house of the LORD and of the royal palace. He took everything, including all the gold shields that Solomon had made.
bsb.14:27: Then King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place and committed them to the care of the captains of the guard on duty at the entrance to the royal palace.
bsb.14:28: And whenever the king entered the house of the LORD, the guards would bear the shields, and later they would return them to the guardroom.
bsb.14:29: As for the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, along with all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
bsb.14:30: There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam throughout their days.
bsb.14:31: And Rehoboam rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the City of David; his mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonite. And his son Abijam reigned in his place.
bsb.15:1: In the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam became king of Judah,
bsb.15:2: and he reigned in Jerusalem three years. His mother’s name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.
bsb.15:3: And Abijam walked in all the sins that his father before him had committed, and his heart was not as fully devoted to the LORD his God as the heart of David his forefather had been.
bsb.15:4: Nevertheless, for the sake of David, the LORD his God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem by raising up a son to succeed him and to make Jerusalem strong.
bsb.15:5: For David had done what was right in the eyes of the LORD and had not turned aside from anything the LORD commanded all the days of his life, except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
bsb.15:6: And there was war between the houses of Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of Abijam’s life.
bsb.15:7: As for the rest of the acts of Abijam, along with all his accomplishments, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah? And there was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.
bsb.15:8: And Abijam rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David, and his son Asa reigned in his place.
bsb.15:9: In the twentieth year of Jeroboam’s reign over Israel, Asa became king of Judah,
bsb.15:10: and he reigned in Jerusalem forty-one years. His grandmother’s name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.
bsb.15:11: And Asa did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as his father David had done.
bsb.15:12: He banished the male shrine prostitutes from the land and removed all the idols that his fathers had made.
bsb.15:13: He also removed his grandmother Maacah from her position as queen mother because she had made a detestable Asherah pole. Asa chopped down the pole and burned it in the Kidron Valley.
bsb.15:14: The high places were not removed, but Asa’s heart was fully devoted to the LORD all his days.
bsb.15:15: And he brought into the house of the LORD the silver and gold and other articles that he and his father had dedicated.
bsb.15:16: Now there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel throughout their days.
bsb.15:17: Baasha king of Israel went to war against Judah and fortified Ramah to prevent anyone from leaving or entering the territory of Asa king of Judah.
bsb.15:18: So Asa withdrew all the silver and gold that remained in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the royal palace. He entrusted it to his servants and sent them with this message to Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon, the son of Hezion king of Aram, who was ruling in Damascus:
bsb.15:19: “Let there be a treaty between me and you, between my father and your father. See, I have sent you a gift of silver and gold. Now go and break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me.”
bsb.15:20: And Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel, conquering Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maacah, and the whole land of Naphtali, including the region of Chinnereth.
bsb.15:21: When Baasha learned of this, he stopped fortifying Ramah and withdrew to Tirzah.
bsb.15:22: Then King Asa summoned all the men of Judah, with no exceptions, and they carried away the stones of Ramah and the timbers Baasha had used for building. And with these materials King Asa built up Geba of Benjamin, as well as Mizpah.
bsb.15:23: Now the rest of the acts of Asa, along with all his might, all his accomplishments, and the cities he built, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah? In his old age, however, he became diseased in his feet.
bsb.15:24: And Asa rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the city of his father David, and his son Jehoshaphat reigned in his place.
bsb.15:25: In the second year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel, and he reigned two years.
bsb.15:26: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD and walked in the way of his father and in his sin, which he had caused Israel to commit.
bsb.15:27: Then Baasha son of Ahijah of the house of Issachar conspired against Nadab, and Baasha struck him down at Gibbethon of the Philistines while Nadab and all Israel were besieging the city.
bsb.15:28: In the third year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Baasha killed Nadab and reigned in his place.
bsb.15:29: As soon as Baasha became king, he struck down the entire household of Jeroboam. He did not leave to Jeroboam anyone that breathed, but destroyed them all according to the word that the LORD had spoken through His servant Ahijah the Shilonite,
bsb.15:30: because of the sins Jeroboam had committed and had caused Israel to commit, and because he had provoked the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger.
bsb.15:31: As for the rest of the acts of Nadab, along with all his accomplishments, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
bsb.15:32: And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel throughout their days.
bsb.15:33: In the third year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king of all Israel, and he reigned in Tirzah twenty-four years.
bsb.15:34: And Baasha did evil in the sight of the LORD and walked in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin, which he had caused Israel to commit.
bsb.16:1: Then the word of the LORD came to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, saying:
bsb.16:2: “Even though I lifted you out of the dust and made you ruler over My people Israel, you have walked in the way of Jeroboam and have caused My people Israel to sin and to provoke Me to anger by their sins.
bsb.16:3: So now I will consume Baasha and his house, and I will make your house like that of Jeroboam son of Nebat:
bsb.16:4: Anyone belonging to Baasha who dies in the city will be eaten by dogs, and anyone who dies in the field will be eaten by the birds of the air.”
bsb.16:5: As for the rest of the acts of Baasha, along with his accomplishments and might, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
bsb.16:6: And Baasha rested with his fathers and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah reigned in his place.
bsb.16:7: Moreover, the word of the LORD came through the prophet Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha and his house, because of all the evil he had done in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him to anger with the work of his hands and becoming like the house of Jeroboam, and also because Baasha had struck down the house of Jeroboam.
bsb.16:8: In the twenty-sixth year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel, and he reigned in Tirzah two years.
bsb.16:9: However, while Elah was in Tirzah getting drunk in the house of Arza the steward of his household there, Elah’s servant Zimri, the commander of half his chariots, conspired against him.
bsb.16:10: So in the twenty-seventh year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Zimri went in, struck Elah down, and killed him. And Zimri reigned in his place.
bsb.16:11: As soon as Zimri began to reign and was seated on the throne, he struck down the entire household of Baasha. He did not leave a single male, whether a kinsman or friend.
bsb.16:12: So Zimri destroyed the entire household of Baasha, according to the word that the LORD had spoken against Baasha through Jehu the prophet.
bsb.16:13: This happened because of all the sins Baasha and his son Elah had committed and had caused Israel to commit, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless idols.
bsb.16:14: As for the rest of the acts of Elah, along with all his accomplishments, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
bsb.16:15: In the twenty-seventh year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Zimri reigned in Tirzah for seven days. Now the troops were encamped against Gibbethon of the Philistines,
bsb.16:16: and the people in the camp heard that Zimri had not only conspired but had also struck down the king. So there in the camp that very day, all Israel proclaimed Omri, the commander of the army, king over Israel.
bsb.16:17: Then Omri and all the Israelites marched up from Gibbethon and besieged Tirzah.
bsb.16:18: When Zimri saw that the city was captured, he entered the citadel of the royal palace and burned it down upon himself. So he died
bsb.16:19: because of the sins he had committed, doing evil in the sight of the LORD and following the example of Jeroboam and the sin he had committed and had caused Israel to commit.
bsb.16:20: As for the rest of the acts of Zimri and the treason he committed, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
bsb.16:21: At that time the people of Israel were divided: Half of the people supported Tibni son of Ginath as king, and half supported Omri.
bsb.16:22: But the followers of Omri proved stronger than those of Tibni son of Ginath. So Tibni died and Omri became king.
bsb.16:23: In the thirty-first year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Omri became king of Israel, and he reigned twelve years, six of them in Tirzah.
bsb.16:24: He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver and built a city there, calling it Samaria after the name of Shemer, who had owned the hill.
bsb.16:25: But Omri did evil in the sight of the LORD and acted more wickedly than all who were before him.
bsb.16:26: For he walked in all the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sins, which he caused Israel to commit, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless idols.
bsb.16:27: As for the rest of the acts of Omri, along with his accomplishments and the might he exercised, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
bsb.16:28: And Omri rested with his fathers and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab reigned in his place.
bsb.16:29: In the thirty-eighth year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria twenty-two years.
bsb.16:30: However, Ahab son of Omri did evil in the sight of the LORD, more than all who were before him.
bsb.16:31: And as if it were not enough for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, he even married Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and he then proceeded to serve and worship Baal.
bsb.16:32: First, Ahab set up an altar for Baal in the temple of Baal that he had built in Samaria.
bsb.16:33: Then he set up an Asherah pole. Thus Ahab did more to provoke the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger than all the kings of Israel before him.
bsb.16:34: In Ahab’s days, Hiel the Bethelite rebuilt Jericho. At the cost of Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundation, and at the cost of Segub his youngest he set up its gates, according to the word that the LORD had spoken through Joshua son of Nun.
bsb.17:1: Now Elijah the Tishbite, who was among the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab, “As surely as the LORD lives—the God of Israel before whom I stand—there will be neither dew nor rain in these years except at my word!”
bsb.17:2: Then a revelation from the LORD came to Elijah:
bsb.17:3: “Leave here, turn eastward, and hide yourself by the Brook of Cherith, east of the Jordan.
bsb.17:4: And you are to drink from the brook, and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.”
bsb.17:5: So Elijah did what the LORD had told him, and he went and lived by the Brook of Cherith, east of the Jordan.
bsb.17:6: The ravens would bring him bread and meat in the morning and evening, and he would drink from the brook.
bsb.17:7: Some time later, however, the brook dried up because there had been no rain in the land.
bsb.17:8: Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah:
bsb.17:9: “Get up and go to Zarephath of Sidon, and stay there. Behold, I have commanded a widow there to provide for you.”
bsb.17:10: So Elijah got up and went to Zarephath. When he arrived at the city gate, there was a widow gathering sticks. Elijah called to her and said, “Please bring me a little water in a cup, so that I may drink.”
bsb.17:11: And as she was going to get it, he called to her and said, “Please bring me a piece of bread.”
bsb.17:12: But she replied, “As surely as the LORD your God lives, I have no bread—only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug. Look, I am gathering a couple of sticks to take home and prepare a meal for myself and my son, so that we may eat it and die.”
bsb.17:13: “Do not be afraid,” Elijah said to her. “Go and do as you have said. But first make me a small cake of bread from what you have, and bring it out to me. Afterward, make some for yourself and your son,
bsb.17:14: for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘The jar of flour will not be exhausted and the jug of oil will not run dry until the day the LORD sends rain upon the face of the earth.’”
bsb.17:15: So she went and did according to the word of Elijah, and there was food every day for Elijah and the woman and her household.
bsb.17:16: The jar of flour was not exhausted and the jug of oil did not run dry, according to the word that the LORD had spoken through Elijah.
bsb.17:17: Later, the son of the woman who owned the house became ill, and his sickness grew worse and worse, until no breath remained in him.
bsb.17:18: “O man of God,” said the woman to Elijah, “what have you done to me? Have you come to remind me of my iniquity and cause the death of my son?”
bsb.17:19: But Elijah said to her, “Give me your son.” So he took him from her arms, carried him to the upper room where he was staying, and laid him on his own bed.
bsb.17:20: Then he cried out to the LORD, “O LORD my God, have You also brought tragedy on this widow who has opened her home to me, by causing her son to die?”
bsb.17:21: Then he stretched himself out over the child three times and cried out to the LORD, “O LORD my God, please let this boy’s life return to him!”
bsb.17:22: And the LORD listened to the voice of Elijah, and the child’s life returned to him, and he lived.
bsb.17:23: Then Elijah took the child, brought him down from the upper room into the house, and gave him to his mother. “Look, your son is alive,” Elijah declared.
bsb.17:24: Then the woman said to Elijah, “Now I know that you are a man of God and that the word of the LORD from your mouth is truth.”
bsb.18:1: After a long time, in the third year of the drought, the word of the LORD came to Elijah: “Go and present yourself to Ahab, and I will send rain upon the face of the earth.”
bsb.18:2: So Elijah went to present himself to Ahab. The famine was severe in Samaria,
bsb.18:3: and Ahab summoned Obadiah, who was in charge of the palace. (Now Obadiah greatly feared the LORD,
bsb.18:4: for when Jezebel had slaughtered the prophets of the LORD, Obadiah had taken a hundred prophets and hidden them, fifty men per cave, providing them with food and water.)
bsb.18:5: Then Ahab said to Obadiah, “Go throughout the land to every spring and every valley. Perhaps we will find grass to keep the horses and mules alive so that we will not have to destroy any livestock.”
bsb.18:6: So they divided the land to explore. Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went the other way by himself.
bsb.18:7: Now as Obadiah went on his way, Elijah suddenly met him. When Obadiah recognized him, he fell facedown and said, “Is it you, my lord Elijah?”
bsb.18:8: “It is I,” he answered. “Go tell your master, ‘Elijah is here!’”
bsb.18:9: But Obadiah replied, “How have I sinned, that you are handing your servant over to Ahab to put me to death?
bsb.18:10: As surely as the LORD your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent someone to search for you. When they said, ‘He is not here,’ he made that kingdom or nation swear that they had not found you.
bsb.18:11: And now you say, ‘Go tell your master that Elijah is here!’
bsb.18:12: I do not know where the Spirit of the LORD may carry you off when I leave you. Then when I go and tell Ahab and he does not find you, he will kill me. But I, your servant, have feared the LORD from my youth.
bsb.18:13: Was it not reported to my lord what I did when Jezebel slaughtered the prophets of the LORD? I hid a hundred prophets of the LORD, fifty men per cave, and I provided them with food and water.
bsb.18:14: And now you say, ‘Go tell your lord that Elijah is here!’ He will kill me!”
bsb.18:15: Then Elijah said, “As surely as the LORD of Hosts lives, before whom I stand, I will present myself to Ahab today.”
bsb.18:16: So Obadiah went to inform Ahab, who went to meet Elijah.
bsb.18:17: When Ahab saw Elijah, he said to him, “Is that you, O troubler of Israel?”
bsb.18:18: “I have not troubled Israel,” Elijah replied, “but you and your father’s house have, for you have forsaken the commandments of the LORD and have followed the Baals.
bsb.18:19: Now summon all Israel to meet me on Mount Carmel, along with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Asherah who eat at Jezebel’s table.”
bsb.18:20: So Ahab summoned all the Israelites and assembled the prophets on Mount Carmel.
bsb.18:21: Then Elijah approached all the people and said, “How long will you waver between two opinions? If the LORD is God, follow Him. But if Baal is God, follow him.” But the people did not answer a word.
bsb.18:22: Then Elijah said to the people, “I am the only remaining prophet of the LORD, but Baal has four hundred and fifty prophets.
bsb.18:23: Get two bulls for us. Let the prophets of Baal choose one bull for themselves, cut it into pieces, and place it on the wood but not light the fire. And I will prepare the other bull and place it on the wood but not light the fire.
bsb.18:24: Then you may call on the name of your god, and I will call on the name of the LORD. The God who answers by fire, He is God.” And all the people answered, “What you say is good.”
bsb.18:25: Then Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, “Since you are so numerous, choose for yourselves one bull and prepare it first. Then call on the name of your god, but do not light the fire.”
bsb.18:26: And they took the bull that was given them, prepared it, and called on the name of Baal from morning until noon, shouting, “O Baal, answer us!” But there was no sound, and no one answered as they leaped around the altar they had made.
bsb.18:27: At noon Elijah began to taunt them, saying, “Shout louder, for he is a god! Perhaps he is deep in thought, or occupied, or on a journey. Perhaps he is sleeping and must be awakened!”
bsb.18:28: So they shouted louder and cut themselves with knives and lances, as was their custom, until the blood gushed over them.
bsb.18:29: Midday passed, and they kept on raving until the time of the evening sacrifice. But there was no response; no one answered, no one paid attention.
bsb.18:30: Then Elijah said to all the people, “Come near to me.” So all the people approached him, and he repaired the altar of the LORD that had been torn down.
bsb.18:31: And Elijah took twelve stones, one for each tribe of the sons of Jacob, to whom the word of the LORD had come and said, “Israel shall be your name.”
bsb.18:32: And with the stones, Elijah built an altar in the name of the LORD. Then he dug a trench around the altar large enough to hold two seahs of seed.
bsb.18:33: Next, he arranged the wood, cut up the bull, placed it on the wood,
bsb.18:34: and said, “Fill four waterpots and pour the water on the offering and on the wood.” “Do it a second time,” he said, and they did it a second time. “Do it a third time,” he said, and they did it a third time.
bsb.18:35: So the water ran down around the altar and even filled the trench.
bsb.18:36: At the time of the evening sacrifice, Elijah the prophet approached the altar and said, “O LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, let it be known this day that You are God in Israel and that I am Your servant and have done all these things at Your command.
bsb.18:37: Answer me, O LORD! Answer me, so that this people will know that You, the LORD, are God, and that You have turned their hearts back again.”
bsb.18:38: Then the fire of the LORD fell and consumed the sacrifice, the wood, the stones, and the dust, and it licked up the water in the trench.
bsb.18:39: When all the people saw this, they fell facedown and said, “The LORD, He is God! The LORD, He is God!”
bsb.18:40: Then Elijah ordered them, “Seize the prophets of Baal! Do not let a single one escape.” So they seized them, and Elijah brought them down to the Kishon Valley and slaughtered them there.
bsb.18:41: And Elijah said to Ahab, “Go up, eat and drink, for there is the sound of a heavy rain.”
bsb.18:42: So Ahab went up to eat and drink. But Elijah climbed to the summit of Carmel, bent down on the ground, and put his face between his knees.
bsb.18:43: “Go and look toward the sea,” he said to his servant. So the servant went and looked, and he said, “There is nothing there.” Seven times Elijah said, “Go back.”
bsb.18:44: On the seventh time the servant reported, “There is a cloud as small as a man’s hand rising from the sea.” And Elijah replied, “Go and tell Ahab, ‘Prepare your chariot and go down before the rain stops you.’”
bsb.18:45: Meanwhile, the sky grew dark with clouds and wind, and a heavy rain began to fall. So Ahab rode away and went to Jezreel.
bsb.18:46: And the hand of the LORD came upon Elijah, and he tucked his cloak into his belt and ran ahead of Ahab all the way to Jezreel.
bsb.19:1: Now Ahab told Jezebel everything that Elijah had done and how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.
bsb.19:2: So Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying, “May the gods deal with me, and ever so severely, if by this time tomorrow I do not make your life like the lives of those you killed!”
bsb.19:3: And Elijah was afraid and ran for his life. When he came to Beersheba in Judah, he left his servant there,
